title: Japanese for the Airport in 9 Comic Scenes | Guess, Listen, Say It (Travel Japanese)
lead: Landing in Japan: immigration, baggage, customs, money exchange and the train into the city, in nine comic scenes. Guess first, then listen twice and say it.

intro.title:
Japan airport
**9 phrases**
intro.say: Nine scenes from landing in Japan. Guess each line before the answer.

phrases.label: Purpose of visit
phrases.when: At immigration, if they ask why you are visiting, answer like this.
phrases.tip: Officers often ask in English too. For work, say shigoto desu.
phrases.hear: 旅行の目的は何ですか？ (Ryokou no mokuteki wa nan desu ka?) = What is the purpose of your trip?
phrases.short: The question you hear at Japan immigration
phrases.scene: At an immigration booth, the staff member, here an immigration officer behind the booth window, holds Jiwoo's passport and asks a question; Jiwoo answers with a bright smile, a camera hanging from her neck; Minjun waits behind a floor line.

phrases.label: How long you stay
phrases.when: If they ask how long you are staying, answer like this.
phrases.tip: Three days is mikkakan, one week is isshuukan. Showing fingers works too.
phrases.hear: 滞在は何日間ですか？ (Taizai wa nan-nichikan desu ka?) = How many days are you staying?
phrases.scene: At the same immigration booth, the officer asks another question; Jiwoo holds up five fingers with her other hand on the booth counter.

phrases.label: Missing bag
phrases.when: If your bag never comes out, tell the staff like this.
phrases.tip: Show the baggage claim tag you got when you checked in.
phrases.scene: Beside an empty, slowly turning baggage carousel, Jiwoo holds up a small baggage claim sticker with a worried face; the staff member on the right leans in to look; Minjun already has his suitcase.

phrases.label: At customs
phrases.when: At customs they ask if you have anything to declare. If not, answer like this.
phrases.tip: If you do, say hai, arimasu. If they ask to open your bag, just open it and show them.
phrases.hear: 申告するものはありますか？ (Shinkoku suru mono wa arimasu ka?) = Anything to declare?
phrases.scene: At a customs counter, the staff member, here a customs officer, asks a question; Jiwoo stands beside her suitcase and shakes her head gently with a polite smile.

phrases.label: Money exchange
phrases.when: Need yen? Ask where to exchange money like this.
phrases.tip: Ryougae means money exchange. Arrival halls usually have exchange counters and ATMs.
phrases.scene: In the arrivals hall, Jiwoo holds a few foreign banknotes and asks the staff member at an information counter, who points to the left with an open hand.

phrases.label: Where to get the train
phrases.ja: 電車はどこから乗れますか？
phrases.pron: Densha wa doko kara noremasu ka?
phrases.ko: Where can I get the train?
phrases.when: Want the train into the city? Ask this.
phrases.tip: At big airports the station is usually downstairs or right next door. Follow the train pictograms.
phrases.short: Find the train from a Japanese airport
phrases.scene: At the information counter, Jiwoo pulls her suitcase and mimes a train with one flat hand gliding forward; the staff member points toward a down escalator.

phrases.label: Asking the fare
phrases.ja: 東京駅までいくらですか？
phrases.ko: How much is it to Tokyo Station?
phrases.when: Want to know the fare? Ask like this.
phrases.tip: Swap in the station you want. Made means up to or as far as.
phrases.scene: At a railway ticket counter in the airport station, Jiwoo leans toward the window and asks; the staff member behind the counter taps a small fare calculator with no readable numbers.

phrases.label: Next train
phrases.ja: 次の電車は何時ですか？
phrases.pron: Tsugi no densha wa nanji desu ka?
phrases.ko: What time is the next train?
phrases.when: Want to know when the next train leaves? Ask this.
phrases.tip: Tsugi no means the next. For a bus: tsugi no basu wa nanji desu ka.
phrases.scene: At the same ticket counter, Jiwoo holds her new ticket and points at her wristwatch with a questioning look; the staff member smiles and gestures toward the platform.

bonus.label: Finding the restroom
bonus.when: Finally, the first thing many people look for at the airport. Ask for the restroom like this.
bonus.scene: In the arrivals hall, Jiwoo shifts from foot to foot with an urgent smile and asks; the staff member points down a corridor with a toilet pictogram; Minjun laughs, holding both suitcases.

outro.title: Recap: **9 phrases**
outro.say: All the phrases are in the description. Tell us in the comments how many you got right. Subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
